Juan Perón. The Argentine military officer and politician who founded Peronism, a nationalist and populist movement that dominated Argentine politics for decades. He served as president three times and created a distinctive political ideology blending labour advocacy, nationalism, and state intervention.

Perón rose to prominence as Labour Minister under Argentina's military junta between 1943 and 1945, building a coalition with labour unions that became his political base. He was elected president in 1946 on a populist platform emphasizing workers' rights, social welfare, and economic nationalism. In 1945, he married actress Eva Perón, who became a beloved public figure and championed his labour policies before her death in 1952. A military coup ousted him in 1955, but he returned to power in 1973 and served until his death, when his second wife Isabel assumed the presidency. Peronism became an enduring political force in Argentina, surviving Perón's death and influencing the nation's politics into the twenty-first century.
